etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English manuel, from Old French manuel, from Late Latin manuāle (“handbook, manual”).

definitions.definition: A booklet that instructs on the usage of a particular machine or product.
(military) A drill in the use of weapons, etc.
(Christianity, historical) An old office-book like the modern Roman Catholic ritual.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English manuel, from Anglo-Norman manuel, Old French manual, from Latin manuālis, from manus (“hand”).

definitions.definition: (of an activity) Performed with the hands.

quote.citation: 1897 October 16, Henry James, What Maisie Knew, Chicago, Ill., New York, N.Y.: Herbert S. Stone & Co., →OCLC:
quote.text: She gave a wild manual brush to her locks.

definitions.definition: (of a machine, device etc.) Operated by means of the hands.
Performed by a human rather than a machine.
(automotive) A manual transmission; a gearbox, especially of a motorized vehicle, shifted by the operator.
(metonymically) A vehicle with a manual transmission.
(music) A keyboard for the hands on a harpsichord, organ, or other musical instrument.
A manual typewriter (as contrasted with an electronic one).
(countable) A device that is operated using the hands, or by a human rather than a machine.
(medicine, colloquial) Manual measurement of the blood pressure, done with a manual sphygmomanometer.
A bicycle technique whereby the front wheel is held aloft by the rider, without the use of pedal force.
A similar maneuver on a skateboard, lifting the front or back wheels while keeping the tail or nose of the board from touching the ground.

quote.citation: 2007, Friedrich von Borries, Steffen P. Walz, Matthias Boettger, editors, Space Time Play: Computer Games, Architecture and Urbanism: The Next Level, 1st edition, Basel: Birkhauser, published 2007, →ISBN, →LCCN, →OCLC, →OL, page 124:
quote.text: In short tutorials, the player learns the basics of skating: reverts, manuals and the ollie – that is, sliding round when coming out of a trick, lifting two wheels off the ground and jumping with the board.

definitions.definition: (countable) A procedure or operation that is done using the hands, or by a human rather than machine.
